### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `sound/hda/hdac_i915.c`**
   - The function `i915_gfx_present()` has been modified to change how it checks for the presence of Intel graphics devices.
   - The previous implementation used `pci_get_class()` to retrieve devices based on the full PCI class bits, which caused issues with matching the i915 graphics device.
   - The new implementation uses a loop with `for_each_pci_dev(display_dev)` to iterate through all PCI devices and checks if the vendor is Intel and if the base class matches `PCI_BASE_CLASS_DISPLAY` (specifically checking the upper 16 bits of the class).
   - The return value of the function has been simplified to return `true` immediately upon finding a matching device, or `false` if no matches are found.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `i915_gfx_present()` directly addresses the regression caused by the previous fix (commit `c9db8a30d9f0`) that incorrectly handled the component binding for i915 GPUs. 
- By changing the method of device discovery from a broad class match to a more specific base class check, the patch ensures that the i915 graphics devices are correctly identified, thus restoring the intended functionality that was lost due to the earlier change.
- The patch is a corrective measure that improves the robustness of the device detection logic, ensuring compatibility with systems that have i915 graphics devices.

Here is the commit message:
ALSA: hda: Fix discovery of i915 graphics PCI device

It's been reported that the recent fix for skipping the
component-binding with D-GPU caused a regression on some systems; it
resulted in the completely missing component binding with i915 GPU.

The problem was the use of pci_get_class() function.  It matches with
the full PCI class bits, while we want to match only partially the PCI
base class bits.  So, when a system has an i915 graphics device with
the PCI class 0380, it won't hit because we're looking for only the
PCI class 0300.

This patch fixes i915_gfx_present() to look up each PCI device and
match with PCI base class explicitly instead of pci_get_class().

Fixes: c9db8a30d9f0 ("ALSA: hda/i915 - skip acomp init if no matching display")
Reviewed-by: Kai Vehmanen <kai.vehmanen@linux.intel.com>
Tested-by: Kai Vehmanen <kai.vehmanen@linux.intel.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Link: https://bugzilla.opensuse.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1200611
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/87bkunztec.wl-tiwai@suse.de
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220621120044.11573-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the use of the `pci_get_class()` function, which matches the full PCI class bits instead of only the PCI base class bits. This led to the failure to detect i915 graphics devices with a PCI class of 0380 when the code was looking for devices with a class of 0300, resulting in missing component binding for the i915 GPU.

Here is the patch:
 /* check whether Intel graphics is present and reachable */
 static int i915_gfx_present(struct pci_dev *hdac_pci)
 {
-	unsigned int class = PCI_BASE_CLASS_DISPLAY << 16;
 	struct pci_dev *display_dev = NULL;
-	bool match = false;
 
-	do {
-		display_dev = pci_get_class(class, display_dev);
-
-		if (display_dev && display_dev->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL &&
+	for_each_pci_dev(display_dev) {
+		if (display_dev->vendor == PCI_VENDOR_ID_INTEL &&
+		    (display_dev->class >> 16) == PCI_BASE_CLASS_DISPLAY &&
 		    connectivity_check(display_dev, hdac_pci)) {
 			pci_dev_put(display_dev);
-			match = true;
+			return true;
 		}
-	} while (!match && display_dev);
+	}
 
-	return match;
+	return false;
 }

